_comment: THE POSTED RULE for the triangle keeper. keeper.py reads every parameter
from this file and accepts none from the command line, so 'it follows a
posted rule' (LAUNCH-DECISIONS.md rule 2) is a property of the code and not
a promise in prose. keeper.py refuses to --arm unless this file is
byte-identical to the copy committed at git HEAD: you cannot arm on an
unpublished rule, and the commit is the timestamp.
Anyone can check the trigger without trusting us:
python3 contracts/triangle_watch.py     # read-only, prints this threshold
Operator sentences of 2026-07-29 recorded here: trigger 4.0%, floor 0.75%,
budget 5,000,000 SCRY, and rule 3 enforced by halt-on-mismatch with no
quiet period. The keeper signs from the dev wallet rather than a dedicated
address; the cost of that choice is that an outside observer cannot separate
keeper trades from treasury moves by watching the address, so rule 4 is
enforced as a spend cap in code (exact-amount approvals, recipient is always
the keeper itself, no transfer-to-third-party path exists) instead of as a
balance you could verify from outside.
WHY THE TRIGGER ALONE DOES NOT DECIDE. Measured 2026-07-29: a 3-leg cycle
pays 2.97% in fees, price impact runs ~0.6% per 100,000 SCRY of size at
current depth, and gas for the cycle is ~$0.015. At a 4.0% gap the best
achievable gross is ~$0.008 -- less than gas. So the gap is a SCREEN and the
binding condition is the quoted net: the keeper solves for size against live
quotes and sends only when the cycle clears both the floor and a multiple of
its own gas. In practice that means it does not fire below roughly 4.4%, and
that number moves with depth and gas rather than being frozen here.

venues._comment: Rule 2: the venues it arbitrages, named. Nothing else is traded.

_comment: Rule 3, the load-bearing one, made mechanical. These are the supply facts
the keeper knows about because they are published HERE. On every run it
re-reads them from chain and halts on any difference -- so minting OBOL or
MYRRH, or posting a ScryHarvest root, stops the keeper until the new figure
is committed to this file. Publishing is therefore a precondition of
trading, not a courtesy that follows it.
Read live with: python3 contracts/keeper.py (any mode prints them).
